title: NPDev semantic relationship graph (npdev-semantic-graph.v1)
description: Path A Phase 2 (P2.2). The model's reference edges relabeled with a semantic verb (Panel reads Concept, Flow calls Procedure, Procedure emits Event, ...) instead of the structural `site` key alone. Produced by com.npdev.dsl.v1.xref.SemanticGraphJson, which relabels com.npdev.dsl.v1.xref.ReferenceIndex's edges rather than computing a second, parallel graph (Decision D1: the semantic layer is a vocabulary and a graph over the existing model, never a parallel model). The generator emits it into each app as npdev/semantic-graph.json. Only RESOLVED edges (see model-xref.schema.json) become graph edges -- an edge naming something that may not exist is model-xref.json's diagnostic concern, not this graph's. Consumers: the Box Inspector (P6.4) and the AI authoring path (P2.4, P7.1), both answering 'what would I reuse for this intent' and 'why does this element exist' from the graph alone.

model.description: How this document names the model it describes -- the model file path for a CLI run, the namespace for a generated app. Free text; nothing parses it.

summary.description: Counts, so a consumer can size the graph without walking it.

nodes.description: Every distinct (kind, name) pair appearing as an edge endpoint, sorted lexicographically by "kind name". The order is part of the contract: this file is emitted into every generated app and hashed across two generator runs by scripts/hygiene/check-deterministic-generation.ps1.

edges.description: Same edges as model-xref.json's `edges` (RESOLVED only), in the same stable order, each carrying a semantic verb instead of (or alongside) the bare structural `site`.

name.description: Qualified name exactly as the composed model spells it. For a `field` node, `Concept.field`.

verb.description: The human-readable relationship: `<from.kind> <verb> <to.kind>` reads as a sentence ("Flow calls Procedure"). One verb per `site` key, defined in SemanticGraphJson.VERBS_BY_SITE; a site with no entry there falls back to the generic "references" so an edge is never silently dropped.

site.description: The structural site this edge came from, carried through unchanged from model-xref.json -- lets a consumer cross-reference the two documents for the same edge.

path.description: Structural pointer to this exact occurrence, carried through unchanged from model-xref.json.
